Hi Alex / Sofia,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the FinCo team. Short recap + next steps from our side.

Summary of what I heard you ask for:
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency for interactive queries <= 350 ms for typical queries, with p99 considered for high-value flows.
- Typical payload: average user input ~1.5k tokens, occasional long docs up to 8k tokens context.
- Output size: usually 100–512 tokens.
- Throughput / concurrency: concurrent interactive users expected to peak ~350 active sessions; baseline expected QPS burst up to ~500 requests/minute (we interpreted as ~8–9 qps sustained, but concurrent sessions matter more for streaming).
- Streaming: yes — partial tokens should be streamed back to the client for low-latency UX.
- Non-functional: encryption at rest/in transit, audit logs, SOC2 (we noted those for Private/Dedicated).

Open questions / clarifications needed from you:
1) For the SLO you stated p95 <= 350 ms — is that for the first byte (TTFB) or for full response finish?
2) What fraction of requests will actually include the full 8k context vs the 1.5k average? A rough distribution helps us size and recommend quantization/batching.
3) Do you need strict p99 SLAs for all flows or only for a small subset of critical transactions?

What we'll do next (from Redwood):
- Send a short follow-up with latency/throughput tradeoffs for different context windows and model sizes (attached: redwood-latency-profiles.pdf).
- Loop in our performance engineer (David Kim) to provide concrete numbers for H100 vs A100 vs L4 and recommended Dedicated pool sizes.
- Propose a canary test: small Dedicated pool + traffic replay using your sample traces (you mentioned you can share).

Next steps for FinCo: share a representative traffic sample (anonymized) and confirm whether the 350 ms target refers to first-byte or end-to-end.

Thanks — I'll be in touch with the detailed numbers shortly.

Best,

Alex / Sofia — thanks, this is super helpful. Looping David in for specific hardware numbers and a recommended Dedicated configuration.

David — quick context: FinCo needs p95 TTFB <= 350 ms for streamed interactive queries. Traffic distribution: 70% <=2k tokens, 25% 2k–6k, 5% >6k (to 8k). Average output length ~256–512 tokens. They will mark ~5% of routes as regulatory (p99 important).

From a product standpoint, a few notes you can call out in the deep-dive:
- Impact of context window: bigger contexts (6–8k) increase KV-cache sizes and memory pressure; that can increase per-token generation latency and reduce batch size efficiency.
- Streaming benefits: first-byte latency is typically lower when we start streaming as soon as partial tokens are available — but total GPU busy time increases slightly.
- Batching tradeoff: larger batches improve throughput (tokens/sec) but increase tail latency. For interactive SLOs we bias toward small batch sizes + autoscaling dedicated pools.

I attached the latency profile PDF with baseline p95 numbers (per-model, per-hardware) — David can correct/expand with measured numbers.

Proposed next steps:
- David to send concrete p95/p99 TTFB numbers for H100/A100/L4 for 512-token outputs with 2k and 8k context samples.
- Agree on canary test plan and data upload.
- Schedule a 30–45m perf deep-dive (please choose 2 slots).

Thanks,
Marissa

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery — perf targets & context window follow-up

Alex / team — thanks for the details. Quick measured numbers (empirical baselines from our perf lab using the same model family you trialed). All numbers are p95 TTFB for a 512-token generation, two different context sizes: 2k and 8k. Measurements assume single-streaming response (we start streaming on first token).

Hardware / model / context | p95 TTFB (512 tokens)
- L4 (small): 2k context -> ~420 ms; 8k context -> ~720 ms
- A100 (16GB perf configs): 2k context -> ~280 ms; 8k context -> ~520 ms
- H100 (large): 2k context -> ~180 ms; 8k context -> ~320 ms

Notes / caveats:
- Batch size: these numbers were collected with low-latency batch settings (batching enabled but small batch cap of 8). For heavy batching (e.g., batch cap 32+) p95 TTFB will increase because the engine waits to accumulate batches; throughput tokens/sec improves.
- Streaming vs full-gen: starting streaming reduces observed TTFB by ~15–25% compared to blocking until full generation, because we send partial tokens as soon as decoding begins. End-to-end time (full response) remains similar or slightly longer for streaming due to decode/flush overheads.
- Concurrency: a single H100 can sustain roughly 60–80 interactive sessions with p95 TTFB ~320–400 ms on the 8k context tail; A100 is ~35–50 sessions for similar quality. These numbers depend heavily on model size and quantization.

Recommended Dedicated pool (to meet p95 TTFB <= 350 ms for your distribution):
- If you want headroom and mostly H100-class performance: 3 H100 GPUs with autoscale policy to +2 on sustained >70% utilization. That supports ~200–240 concurrent interactive sessions with good headroom; add more for spikes.
- If you prefer cost-savings with A100s: 6 A100s with more aggressive autoscaling and smaller batch caps.
- For strict p99/regulatory flows: isolate those routes onto a separate pool (canary) to avoid noisy neighbor effects and guarantee lower tail latency.

Attachments: I uploaded a short CSV with example throughput simulations (finco-metrics-sample.csv) to the Drive link.

Next actions I recommend:
1) Run a traffic replay against a small Dedicated canary (2 H100s) with your sanitized trace and confirm p95/p99.
2) If the trace is representative, we can produce a cost + capacity plan for a production pool (3–4 H100s).
3) We'll instrument streaming-first-byte metrics so you can map TTFB to UX events.

Happy to discuss tomorrow — I'm available 10:00–12:00 and 15:00–17:00 PT.

—David
